message.content: {"results":[{"n":"G1","evidence":"All five screenshots show the 3D bamboo scene rendering properly in Chrome without errors or a blank screen.","pass":true},{"n":"G2","evidence":"OrbitControls allows dragging, but there is no polar angle restriction in the code to prevent going below the ground, and screenshot 5 shows the camera zooming completely outside the grove (controls.maxDistance = 45 exceeds the ~21.5m grove radius).","pass":false},{"n":"G3","evidence":"The scene uses only two InstancedMeshes (340 stalks and 3400 leaf planes), one 2048x2048 shadow map, and a single UnrealBloomPass, which will easily exceed 30 fps on standard integrated graphics.","pass":true},{"n":"1","evidence":"All screenshots show a persistent UI bar at the bottom left with hint text and three interactive buttons ('Match Photo Angle', 'Ground Walk View', 'Wind: ON').","pass":false},{"n":"2","evidence":"In the animate() loop, windUniforms.uTime is updated automatically on load while windOn defaults to true, driving vertex shader sway on stalks and leaves without user input.","pass":true},{"n":"3","evidence":"Screenshot 1 matches the reference photo's dramatic upward-looking wide-angle perspective, with converging foreground bamboo stalks and a dark overhanging branch in the upper left.","pass":true},{"n":"4","evidence":"Screenshots 1–3 show tightly spaced foreground and midground bamboo stalks that closely match the dense spacing in the reference photo.","pass":true},{"n":"5","evidence":"While the green hues of the stalks and leaves are close to the photo, the scene is heavily washed out by bright white fog/halation across the frame (screenshots 1–3), losing the deep green contrast of the photo.","pass":false},{"n":"6","evidence":"Neither the reference photo (an upward canopy shot) nor the 3D scene contains a path or brushwood fence; the code only places a plain dark green CircleGeometry for the ground.","pass":false},{"n":"7","evidence":"Both the photo and screenshots 1–3 feature bright diffuse/overcast zenith sky light filtering down from directly above the canopy.","pass":true},{"n":"8","evidence":"Screenshots 1–3 clearly show dark horizontal node rings with slight geometric ridges at regular intervals along the bamboo stalks.","pass":true},{"n":"9","evidence":"In the stalk placement loop and screenshots 1–3, culms vary in thickness (scaleR from 0.68 to 1.25) and height (scaleY from 0.82 to 1.14).","pass":true},{"n":"10","evidence":"Screenshots 1–3 and the instancing setup show stalks leaning at varied angles and curving organically rather than standing in a rigid vertical grid.","pass":true},{"n":"11","evidence":"Screenshot 4 clearly shows the canopy constructed from clusters of thin, narrow lanceolate bamboo leaves arranged in fans on slender stems.","pass":true},{"n":"12","evidence":"In section 9 of the code, the ground is simply a flat untextured CircleGeometry with a solid color (0x1a2616), with no soil texture or fallen leaves.","pass":false},{"n":"13","evidence":"Screenshot 5 (zoomed out) reveals the entire bamboo grove as a finite circular patch surrounded by empty white space, showing clear outer edges.","pass":false},{"n":"14","evidence":"Leaf instances have castShadow left as false, so no dappled sunlight patches are cast onto the stalks or ground in screenshots 1–3.","pass":false},{"n":"15","evidence":"Screenshots 1–3 show strong atmospheric haze/bloom between the stalks, creating depth separation from foreground to canopy, though somewhat overblown.","pass":true},{"n":"16","evidence":"In screenshots 1–4, upper leaves against the bright sky appear bright yellow-green via emissive mapping, giving the visual impression of backlit glowing foliage.","pass":true},{"n":"17","evidence":"Because of the HemisphereLight (intensity 1.85) and green bounceLight, shaded areas between stalks in screenshots 1–4 retain dark green tones and never turn pure black.","pass":true},{"n":"18","evidence":"While stalks have a sheen and subtle powdery bands near nodes, screenshots 1–3 show uniform green tubes lacking natural yellowing, distinct stains, or varied weathering across culms.","pass":false},{"n":"19","evidence":"In screenshot 4, the leaf planes look completely opaque and flatly shaded when viewed up close, using only alphaTest cutouts and uniform emissive color rather than true translucency.","pass":false},{"n":"20","evidence":"The ground is never textured as soil, leaves, or stone; the code defines groundMat as a solid-color MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x1a2616 }).","pass":false},{"n":"21","evidence":"Because the default camera pitches sharply upward toward y=14.5, perspective causes verticals to converge cleanly toward the zenith with no unintended camera roll or tilt (screenshot 1).","pass":true},{"n":"22","evidence":"In leafMat.onBeforeCompile, vertex positions are displaced horizontally using sin(uTime * 0.85 + ...) and a faster flutter term, making the canopy sway continuously.","pass":true},{"n":"23","evidence":"In bambooMat.onBeforeCompile, horizontal wind displacement is multiplied by pow(hFactor, 2.1) where hFactor is normalized height, so bases stay fixed while tops bend.","pass":true},{"n":"24","evidence":"In both bambooMat and leafMat vertex shaders, uWindStrength is a constant 1.0 and motion is driven purely by fixed-frequency sine/cosine waves with no gust modulation over time.","pass":false},{"n":"25","evidence":"There is no particle system, falling leaf geometry, or drifting dust implemented anywhere in the HTML source or visible in the screenshots.","pass":false},{"n":"26","evidence":"Driven continuously by clock.getElapsedTime() with gentle frequencies (0.72 and 0.85 rad/s, ~7–8 second periods) and amplitudes (~0.3m at 28m height), motion runs smoothly at realistic speed without loop resets.","pass":true},{"n":"27","evidence":"Every stalk shares the exact same geometry with a hardcoded curve (curveX = Math.pow(vNorm, 1.85) * 0.65) and identical repeating canvas texture, though varied Y-rotations and scales keep cloning from being blatantly obvious in screenshots 1–3; however, identical node markings repeat visibly on adjacent hero stalks in screenshot 1.","pass":false},{"n":"28","evidence":"Leaves use alphaTest: 0.32 with depth writes enabled and there are no LOD transitions or billboards, preventing alpha-sorting pop-in or flicker when orbiting.","pass":true},{"n":"29","evidence":"In screenshots 1–4, large 2.7x2.7m leaf planes are placed randomly around stalk anchors and visibly intersect and clip right through nearby bamboo culms.","pass":false},{"n":"30","evidence":"Screenshot 1 looks distinctly like real-time 3D graphics at first glance due to the washed-out white fog, repetitive painted node rings, plastic specular highlights on stalks, and crude tubular tree branch in the upper left (plus the UI bar).","pass":false}]}
